title: Fleet overview ($cluster)
description: Is anything wrong, and where? Firing alerts, then one row of health tiles per cluster and one line of tiles per platform component. Every tile opens the drill-down view for that cluster and namespace, or the component's dashboard.

links.title: Fleet overview
links.tooltip: The home page: is anything wrong, and where?

links.title: Kubernetes views
links.tooltip: Cluster, namespace and pod drill-down views

panels.title: Critical alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing with severity critical. Anything above zero needs a person now: open the table beside it, start with the oldest.

panels.title: Warning alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing with severity warning. Not urgent, but a warning that stays is a critical in waiting: assign it before it escalates.

panels.title: Other alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing with any other severity (info or unset). Read them for context; they never page anyone.

panels.title: Firing alerts over time
panels.description: How many alerts fired, by severity, over the selected range. A step up is a new incident; a slow rise is an accumulating backlog.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Every alert firing now in the selected clusters and namespaces, from the store's own ALERTS series. Start with the critical ones; the Alert cell opens the namespace's view. An alert with no namespace is about the cluster itself.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Critical and warning alerts firing for this cluster. Above zero: read the table at the top, filtered to this cluster.

panels.title: Pods not Ready
panels.description: Pods that are Pending or Running but not Ready (Succeeded pods, such as finished Jobs, are excluded). Open the namespaces view and read Pods with unexpected status.

targets.expr: count((kube_pod_status_ready{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",condition="false"} == 1) and on (k8s_cluster_name, namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1)) or vector(0)

panels.title: CrashLoopBackOff
panels.description: Containers currently waiting in CrashLoopBackOff: the process starts and dies. Read the pod's logs and its last terminated reason in the pod view.

panels.title: ImagePullBackOff
panels.description: Containers that cannot pull their image (ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull). Check the image name and tag, the registry, and the pull secret.

panels.title: Restarts (1h)
panels.description: Container restarts in the last hour. A handful is noise; a steady climb is a crash loop or OOM kills. Open the namespaces view and read Container Restarts.

panels.title: Nodes NotReady
panels.description: Nodes whose Ready condition is false or unknown. Pods on them are unreachable or about to be evicted: check the node's kubelet and the cloud instance.

panels.title: Nodes under pressure
panels.description: Nodes reporting memory, disk or PID pressure. The kubelet starts evicting pods under pressure: find the noisy workload in the cluster view, or add capacity.

panels.title: PVCs over 85% full
panels.description: Persistent volumes whose used bytes exceed 85% of capacity. Expand the claim or clean up before it fills; open the namespaces view for the Persistent Volumes panels.

panels.title: Rows dropped or ignored (1h)
panels.description: Rows the metrics, logs and traces stores refused in the last hour (ignored or dropped for a reason, such as too many labels or a timestamp out of range). Above zero means data is being lost at the write path: open the store dashboard and read the reason.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(vm_rows_ignored_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}[1h])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(vl_rows_dropped_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}[1h])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(vt_rows_dropped_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}[1h])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Kargo stages not healthy
panels.description: Kargo Stages whose Ready or Healthy condition is false or unknown. Shows n/a where the Kargo state metrics are not enabled. Open the Stage in Kargo and read its conditions.

panels.title: Kargo promotions errored
panels.description: Errored Promotions whose Stage has not recovered (the same condition the KargoPromotionErrored alert uses). Shows n/a where the Kargo state metrics are not enabled. Re-promote once the cause is fixed.

panels.title: Pods running
panels.description: Pods in the Running phase, for scale. It is context, not an alarm: a sudden drop with no deploy is worth a look.

panels.title: Rows ingested per second, by store
panels.description: The store write path: rows per second accepted by the metrics (vm_), logs (vl_) and traces (vt_) components of this cluster. A flat zero on a store that had traffic means the write path is dead; the WritePathDead alert watches the same counters.

panels.title: Rows dropped or ignored per second, by store
panels.description: Rows the stores refused, by reason. Should be flat at zero. A rise means data loss at ingest: read the reason label, then fix the sender (label count, timestamps) or the store limit.

panels.title: ArgoCD apps not Synced
panels.description: Applications whose sync status is anything but Synced: Git and the cluster disagree. Open the ArgoCD dashboard, then the application, and read the sync result. n/a where ArgoCD is not scraped.

panels.title: ArgoCD apps not Healthy
panels.description: Applications whose health is anything but Healthy (Progressing, Degraded, Missing, Suspended, Unknown). A few Progressing during a rollout is normal; one that stays is not. n/a where ArgoCD is not scraped.

panels.title: ArgoCD targets down
panels.description: ArgoCD metrics endpoints (application controller, API server, repo server) that stopped answering. Any down leaves that part of ArgoCD unobserved, and the two tiles beside it stale.

panels.title: Certificates expiring in 14 days
panels.description: Certificates that expire within 14 days (certificates with no expiry yet, still being issued, are not counted). One that has not renewed means its issuer or challenge is failing: open the cert-manager dashboard and read the Ready condition. n/a where cert-manager is not scraped.

panels.title: Certificates not Ready
panels.description: Certificates whose Ready condition is false or unknown. A new certificate is not Ready until issued; one that stays so is stuck. Open the cert-manager dashboard's Certificates table.

panels.title: cert-manager targets down
panels.description: cert-manager metrics endpoints (controller, cainjector) that stopped answering. Certificates are not being renewed while the controller is down.

panels.title: NATS servers down
panels.description: NATS metrics endpoints that stopped answering: the server or its exporter is down. Publishers and consumers on that server are affected. n/a where NATS is not scraped.

panels.title: JetStream disabled
panels.description: NATS servers reporting JetStream as disabled. Streams and durable consumers need it: a server that should have it and does not is misconfigured or restarted without its store.

panels.title: NATS slow consumers (1h)
panels.description: Slow consumers the servers reported in the last hour: clients that could not keep up and were disconnected or lost messages. Find the client and raise its limit or speed it up.

panels.title: Envoy 5xx per second
panels.description: Requests per second the proxies answered with a 5xx, measured at the client side. Near zero is healthy; open the Envoy proxy dashboard, then the Envoy clusters dashboard to find the failing backend. n/a where the proxies are not scraped.

panels.title: Envoy 5xx share of requests
panels.description: Share of client requests the proxies answered with a 5xx, over five minutes. Above 1% is worth a look; above 5% is an outage for some route.

panels.title: Envoy proxies down
panels.description: Envoy proxy metrics endpoints that stopped answering. A proxy pod that is down serves no traffic; check the Gateway's pods.

panels.title: CNPG operator reconcile errors (1h)
panels.description: Reconciles that ended in an error in the last hour, across the CloudNativePG operator's control loops. A few are retried conflicts; a steady count means a Postgres cluster, backup or pooler cannot converge. n/a where the operator is not scraped.

panels.title: CNPG operator down
panels.description: CloudNativePG operator metrics endpoints that stopped answering. With the operator down no Postgres cluster is reconciled: failovers and backups are not driven.

panels.title: Postgres instances up
panels.description: Postgres instances whose exporter answers and reports up; with the tile beside it they add up to every instance the cluster scrapes. Zero where instances exist means none is reachable. n/a where the instance metrics are not scraped (the optional cnpg-instance-metrics source).

panels.title: Postgres instances not up
panels.description: Postgres instances that are scraped but report down: the pod is starting, failing, or its database does not answer. Open the instances dashboard and read Instance ready, then the pod's events.

panels.title: Postgres replication lag (max)
panels.description: The largest replication lag any scraped standby reports, in seconds. Near zero is healthy; a lag that grows means a standby cannot keep up and a failover would lose that much.

panels.title: Newest Postgres backup age
panels.description: Age of the newest successful backup across the scraped Postgres clusters, from the backup plugin's own timestamp. Past a day and a half means a scheduled backup was missed: read the Backup resources. n/a where no backup is reported.
